subject: biology
title: Ecology Adventure 1: Energy flow and food webs
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace energy through ecosystems — and lose 90% at each step.
meta_desc: Biology Ecology — producers, consumers, decomposers, food webs, 10% energy transfer.
final_note: You learned producers fix solar energy, ~10% transfers between trophic levels, and pyramids show energy loss as heat.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Energy flows one way:

Sun → producers (plants, algae, cyanobacteria) → primary consumers (herbivores) → secondary → tertiary.

Decomposers (fungi, bacteria) recycle nutrients from dead matter back to producers.

Only ~10% of energy passes between trophic levels. The rest is lost as:
- Heat (respiration)
- Undigested matter (egestion)
- Movement

This caps food chains at 4-5 levels. NPP = GPP − respiration. Tropical rainforests have highest NPP (~2200 g m⁻² yr⁻¹).

Pyramid of energy (units: kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹) always shrinks upward — second law of thermodynamics.

Pyramid of biomass usually shrinks but can invert (e.g. ocean plankton — small but rapid turnover).

Pyramid of numbers can be inverted (one tree → many insects).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a silent and a missense mutation?
options: Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.
A silent mutation changes a base but the codon still codes for the same amino acid; a missense mutation changes the amino acid encoded.
Stem cells are simply cells that haven't grown big enough yet.
A silent mutation has no effect because no base actually changes.

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.
